correctness.rationale: For any symmetric spider determinant, a corank-one adjugate has some nonzero diagonal cofactor, proving the exact singular corank-two criterion. The path recurrence shows that a nonzero-edge spider component has nullity at least two precisely with at least three singular arms; zero-edge forest decomposition forces either a two-sided cut or a central triple, proving exhaustiveness even on special strata. The generic tree determinant is irreducible by primitive leaf expansion. Disjoint-variable equations give prime complete intersections and degrees. Rational witnesses establish surjectivity of the kernel-restricted three-dimensional quadratic variation map on each irreducible component; Schur complement and formal Morse lemma give generic nodes. Codimension-two singular support and hypersurface S2 give normality. The standard-library checker independently exhausts 218700 small configurations and verifies exact-rational corank-two quadratic variation witnesses; finite tests are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Closest primary literature covers general symmetric determinants (Kerner--Vinnikov), real Hermitian tree-eigenvalue branch assignments, and generic symmetric multilinear forms (Huang). Previous local records describe only pure star/arrowhead and pure path/tridiagonal patterns. None of those inspected statements gives a scheme-theoretic reduced-support classification for nonstar spiders with internal arm edges, all edge-zero boundary cases, their distinct prime component ideals, and weighted individual degrees. Aggregate degree and generic corank-two local-determinant behavior are not claimed as independent discoveries. Historical unindexed coverage is possible.
residual_risks: A classical or unindexed treatment of sparse symmetric spider determinants could contain the same component equations.

value.rationale: Spider graphs are a standard, naturally defined infinite class with heterogeneous arm lengths, and the associated sparse symmetric determinant is a canonical singular projective hypersurface. The result provides a complete reduced singular-support decomposition, separate prime defining equations and exact degrees, with normality and the transverse singularity type for every generic component. This is finer than the global corank-two cycle degree and the special star/path cases, and supports future calculations of strata, intersection behavior, and divisorial invariants. It does not depend on an arbitrary cut-off, small increase, numerical coincidence, or unsupported downstream theorem.
